title: When The Whole Neighborhood Gets Arrested
description:
Submit a tip! Tips@Midwest-Safety.com

Please consider JOINING for $1 a month. It *really* helps us do original reporting like this. 

CONTACT US:
Complaints? Video submissions? Sponsorships? Collabs? Business inquires? 
Email our board at Tips@Midwest-Safety.com

BE NICE:
The individuals presented in these videos may be suffering from the effects of alcohol, drug abuse, a mental health disorder or simply having a bad day. The videos should NOT be presumed to be representative of their general behavior. Everyone deserves to be treated with respect. 

RIGHT TO BE FORGOTTEN:
Midwest Safety practices the "Right to be Forgotten." If you were the suspect in a lower-level offense, you may email our board to request removal. 
Email: mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com

The female suspect who started this whole incident, Christina, who also works for the Glades County Sheriff's Department in Florida, was charged with felony battery, breach of peace, and felony resisting with violence. As part of a plea agreement, the judge chose not to prosecute on the charges of breach of peace and resisting with violence. The battery charge resulted in a withhold of adjudication, meaning the judge accepted Christina's no contest plea, but decided not to formally convict her. She was sentenced to one year of probation. Her husband, Wesley, the man who bulldozed through the officer, was charged with felony battery, resisting obstructing without violence, breach of peace, and felony assault on a law enforcement officer. The judge found him guilty of all charges, and subsequently sentenced him to a concurrent sentence of one year of probation for all four charges. Antonio, the third person arrested, was charged with felony possession of a controlled substance, resisting obstructing without violence and breach of peace. The judge dropped all three of his charges. His wife, Maria, was charged with resisting obstructing without violence, disorderly conduct, and violation of probation. While the charges of disorderly conduct and violation of probation were dismissed, her resisting obstructing charge resulted in adjudication withheld, and she was subsequently sentenced to six months of probation.
